$comment: 01.7.1-T4.2 (AC6): vulnerability-scan allowlist consumed by scripts/audit-deps.sh and scripts/audit_deps_eval.py. Keyed by advisory id (GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz or CVE-YYYY-NNNNN — the last path segment of the advisory URL from 'npm audit --json' or 'dotnet list package --vulnerable --format json'). Every entry must name the accepting ADR (adr), the affected package, and the reason; 'expires' (YYYY-MM-DD, parsed as a real date) is optional for an unscoped entry but REQUIRED once 'scope' is present — an expired, undated or unparseable date never exempts. 'scope' is optional and npm-only: {"npm": [{"workspace": "<workspace name>", "via": "<direct dependency>"}]} narrows the exemption to those (origin, direct dependency) pairs over the package-lock.json graph. Enforced: only a lockfileVersion 3 lock is read; every production chain from the root package or from a record outside node_modules/ must start with a listed pair, and only a workspace the lock's root record declares may satisfy one (patterns are normalised for a leading ./ and trailing /, matched per path segment so * never crosses /, and negation, braces, extglob, ** or escapes exit 2; a workspace record without name cannot satisfy a pair). The 'via' must be the un-followed record where npm installed it: under node_modules/, not link: true, real name equal to the pair, resolved under https://registry.npmjs.org/<name>/-/ and an integrity hash present. npm audit's 'nodes' for the advisory must be non-empty and every node must be a record the walk reaches. Anything the lock cannot prove — unreadable or non-v3 lock, a required edge with no record (including a target's own), a record that is not an object, an audit node the lock does not reach, any unexpected error — is a scanner failure (exit 2), never an exemption. Limits: the scope constrains those two hops only (it does not show how the package is invoked), the walk trusts the lock's records exactly as npm ci does, the registry host is hard-coded so a mirror fails closed, and the exception files are PR-editable, so review of this file, the gate scripts and the lock is the real control. An unscoped entry behaves as before: advisory id plus a live ADR is enough.
